description: These spreadsheets track how often patients in United States hospitals catch infections linked to their care, and how intensively devices such as catheters and ventilators are used, nationally and state by state. The producer is the National Healthcare Safety Network of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, which compiles reports from hospitals in its Patient Safety Component and publishes an annual progress report. Coverage runs from 2009 to 2024, with separate files for acute care hospitals, critical access hospitals, inpatient rehabilitation facilities, long-term acute care hospitals and national pediatric and oncology units. Each file gives standardized infection ratios, comparing observed with predicted infections, and standardized utilization ratios for device days, with a new statistical baseline from 2015. The files are available as a free download from the CDC website, and archived years carry DOIs in the CDC Stacks repository, as public domain federal works. Caveats: state and national aggregates, not individual hospitals, ratios before and after 2015 use different baselines, and COVID-19 disrupted recent years. Simulation uses: setting infection risk and device demand in hospital capacity models, and measuring how surges such as pandemics degrade the quality of care. Related records: the RKI emergency department surveillance (data-rki-emergency-department-surveillance) gives a German view of hospital system strain.

schema_summary: Annual national and state Standardized Infection Ratios (SIR, observed versus predicted infections) and Standardized Utilization Ratios (SUR, device days versus predicted) for healthcare-associated infections and device use, separately for acute care hospitals, critical access hospitals, inpatient rehabilitation facilities, long-term acute care hospitals and national pediatric and oncology locations

sources.note: HAI Progress Reports page: annual reports use NHSN Patient Safety Component data to present national and state HAI SIRs and SURs; SIRs and SURs 2009-2014 under the original baseline, 2015 baseline from 2015; data for 2009 to 2024 (current); 2024 SIR data files for acute care hospitals, critical access hospitals, inpatient rehabilitation facilities, long-term acute care hospitals, pediatric and oncology (XLS); 2024 SUR data for the same facility types; brief report on quarterly national SIRs in 2022
